lines.text: This is Ground. *Open* *Hatch* *3.*
I didn't answer. Rule three.
Then it said my name.
Cole. Open Hatch 3.
The next day, at seven, the same call. And the next. And the next.
Always seven o'clock. Always the same words.
I asked Ground on channel 4: did you call me on channel 9?
Ground copies. Continue.
So I read the station manual.
Channel 9 is the intercom between modules. It doesn't even reach the Earth.
Whoever was calling me was wired into this station.
Someone up here knew my name. And wanted that hatch open.
Day one hundred twenty. Envelope four.
Panel 12. The oxygen generator. You'll need it sooner than they told you.
Behind panel 12 was a machine that splits water into oxygen.
I turned it on.
The oxygen stopped falling. The water started falling faster.
From now on, my water was also my air.
Day one hundred fifty. Envelope five.
If the power ever fails: suit 2. It's the good one.
I checked suit 2. Just in case.
Day one hundred fifty-one. Six in the morning. The numbers.
Oxygen, 113. Water, 64. Power... 31 percent.
The main solar array had stopped turning.
No power, no oxygen generator.
Without the generator, the oxygen would last sixty-six days. The ship was two hundred fourteen days away.
Then the lights went *out.*
